recipes.name: Lean Fish and Vegetable Curry (Macher Jhol)
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is rich in Omega-3 fatty acids and Vitamin D from fatty fish like Rohu or Tilapia, which may help improve LDL cholesterol levels and address Vitamin D deficiency. The vegetables add fiber and essential nutrients. Cooking with mustard oil provides healthy monounsaturated fats.
instructions: Lightly pan-fry fish fillets in 1 tbsp mustard oil until golden brown. Set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining mustard oil. Sauté chopped onion until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chili, cumin, and coriander powder. Cook until oil separates.
Add cubed potatoes and cauliflower (if using), green chilies, and salt. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Add water and bring to a simmer. Cook until vegetables are tender.
Gently add the fried fish fillets to the curry. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: High-Fiber Masoor Dal Tadka with Spinach
recipes.health_benefit: This dal is an excellent source of soluble fiber, which can help bind to cholesterol and reduce LDL levels. Spinach adds essential vitamins, minerals, and additional fiber. It's a low-fat, nutrient-dense option that supports cardiovascular health.
instructions: Wash masoor dal thoroughly and pressure cook with 3 cups of water, turmeric powder, and salt for 3-4 whistles or until soft and mushy.
Once the dal is cooked, open the lid and add the chopped spinach. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until the spinach wilts.
For the tadka: Heat ghee in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Let them splutter.
Add asafoetida, chopped onion, and green chili. Sauté until onion turns golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato and red chili powder (if using). Cook until tomatoes are soft.
Pour the tadka over the cooked dal. Stir well.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Oats Upma with Mixed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: Oats are well-known for their soluble fiber (beta-glucan), which effectively helps reduce LDL cholesterol. This Upma is packed with various vegetables, increasing the fiber content and providing essential vitamins and minerals, contributing to overall cardiovascular health.
instructions: Dry roast the rolled oats in a pan for 2-3 minutes until lightly toasted. Set aside.
In the same pan, heat mustard oil. Add mustard seeds and curry leaves. Let them splutter.
Add chopped onion, green chili (if using), and grated ginger. Sauté until onion turns translucent.
Add carrots, peas, and capsicum. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender.
Add turmeric powder and mix well.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring it to a boil.
Once boiling, add the roasted oats, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes, until oats absorb the water and are cooked.
Turn off the heat, add lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves. Mix gently and serve hot.

recipes.name: Baked Chicken and Vegetable Skewers
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe offers lean protein from chicken, which is important for overall health without adding unhealthy fats that could negatively impact LDL. The abundant vegetables provide fiber, vitamins, and minerals. Baking or grilling minimizes fat, making it a heart-healthy choice.
instructions: In a bowl, combine chicken cubes with ginger-garlic paste, low-fat yogurt, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, lemon juice, mustard oil, and salt. Mix well and marinate for at least 15-20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Thread the marinated chicken and vegetables (bell peppers, onion, cherry tomatoes) alternately onto the skewers.
Place the skewers on the prepared baking tray.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, flipping halfway through, or until the chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Serve hot with a side of mint chutney or a simple cucumber salad.

recipes.name: Ragi Dosa with Vegetable Sambhar
recipes.prep_time: 20 mins (plus fermentation time for dosa batter)
recipes.health_benefit: Ragi (finger millet) is a whole grain rich in fiber and beneficial compounds that may help in managing blood sugar and cholesterol levels. The vegetable-rich Sambhar adds additional fiber, vitamins, and minerals. This is a gluten-free and heart-healthy breakfast option.
instructions: For Dosa Batter: Grind soaked urad dal with a little water to a smooth paste. Mix with ragi flour, rice flour, and enough water to make a thin pouring consistency batter. Add salt and let it ferment for 6-8 hours or overnight.
For Sambhar: Pressure cook toor dal with chopped vegetables until soft. Mash lightly.
In a pan, heat 1 tsp oil. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and sauté until soft. Add chopped tomato and cook until mushy.
Add sambhar powder and tamarind pulp. Mix well.
Add the cooked dal-vegetable mixture to the pan. Add water to achieve desired consistency. Simmer for 10-15 minutes.
To make Dosa: Heat a non-stick tawa. Pour a ladleful of ragi dosa batter and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin dosa.
Drizzle a few drops of mustard oil around the edges. Cook until golden brown and crisp. Flip and cook briefly on the other side if needed.
Serve hot Ragi Dosa with the vegetable-rich Sambhar.

recipes.name: Mackerel/Salmon Pan Fry with Steamed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: Mackerel and Salmon are excellent sources of Vitamin D and Omega-3 fatty acids, both of which are crucial for improving Vitamin D status and managing LDL cholesterol. Pan-frying with minimal healthy oil and pairing with steamed vegetables makes this a lean, nutrient-dense, and heart-healthy meal.
instructions: Marinate the fish fillet with lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chili powder, cumin powder, and salt for 10-15 minutes.
While the fish marinates, steam the broccoli, carrots, and green beans until tender-crisp. Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Heat mustard oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Place the marinated fish fillet in the hot pan and pan-fry for 4-6 minutes on each side, or until cooked through and nicely browned.
Serve the pan-fried mackerel/salmon immediately with the side of steamed vegetables.
